concerns.text: SC-005 requires uniformity of p-values 'simulated on random data' — i.e. a validation of the TEST on data known to satisfy the null. Phase 5.1 instead runs the KS test on the raw p-values from the actual Möbius data. That conflates test validation with the research result itself: if Chowla/random-sign fails, the KS test will (correctly) reject uniformity, and the pipeline would report the test as 'inconsistent'. Add a separate calibration step (KS on p-values from permuted/simulated windows) distinct from the empirical KS on real data.

'σ² = (6/π²)(1 − 6/π²) ≈ 0.6079' — the numeric value is wrong: 6/π² ≈ 0.6079, but the product (6/π²)(1−6/π²) ≈ 0.2384. This also propagates to the power claim (SE ≈ 0.0032 at L=10⁵ corresponds to √(1/L), not √(σ²/L) ≈ 0.0015). Fix the constant and reconcile the SE/power statement with the stated variance model.

'significant_change = true iff any lag flips significance (p < 0.05, raw)' — with 1,000 permutations, p-values near 0.05 have Monte Carlo noise ≈ ±0.007, so borderline lags will flip by resampling chance alone, inflating 'sensitive' flags. The plan should either use adjusted p-values, require flips exceeding the permutation resolution, or acknowledge MC noise as a limitation; otherwise the sensitivity metric partly measures resampling noise, not zero-density robustness.
